$comment: price.regime@1.0.0 — source §8.4. Every 'ok' case is a flat 20-session close series (close_0..close_19 = 100) with a single move on the final session, chosen so the realized volatility stays under the 0.005 floor — the outer clamp then acts on 0.6·r5+0.4·r20 divided by a fixed 0.005, which is hand-computable exactly. Sign/magnitude-only checks (not exact strings) cover the branch where volatility exceeds the floor, in the companion test file, because that branch is genuinely irrational (sqrt).

abstention.message: The price series is tagged 'intraday', not 'adjusted_close'. Source §8.4 requires adjusted daily closes for regime calculations and forbids mixing intraday and close-to-close returns in the same metric — this is a registry-level prohibition, not a preference, so the computation stops rather than mix quote kinds.
One of the closes in the window is zero or negative, which is not a real traded price. A regime computed across a bad price would be a fabricated number.

cases.name: floor_engaged_at_clamp_bound
cases.why: A 1.5% move on the final session against 20 flat closes: r5 = r20 = 0.015, realized volatility ≈ 0.00327 (well under the 0.005 floor), (0.6·0.015+0.4·0.015)/0.005 = 3 exactly — at the clamp bound, not past it.

cases.name: exceeds_upper_clamp
cases.why: A 2% move: r5 = r20 = 0.02, realized volatility ≈ 0.00436 (still under the floor), raw trend ratio = 4, clamped to 3 before the final /3 — same numeric result as the boundary case, reached by the clamp instead of landing on it exactly.

cases.name: negative_at_clamp_bound
cases.why: The mirror of floor_engaged_at_clamp_bound: a −1.5% move gives trend_strength exactly −1.
